newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S POLITICIANS GET NEW PAY PROPOSALS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S POLITICIANS GET NEW PAY PROPOSALS.

text.p: South Africa's politicians should get pay rises of up to 22 percent, a commission appointed by President Nelson Mandela said on Thursday.

The commission, headed by judge Jan Steyn, told a news conference that ordinary members of parliament should get an 8.0 percent increase to 239,623 rand a year ($52,000) and cabinet ministers should get a 12 percent hike to 474,713 rand.
The biggest increase recommended was for deputy speakers of provincial legislatures, who the commission said should get 22 percent more for a total of 350,860 rand.
"We have sought to structure all aspects of remuneration in such a manner as to promote good, clean government and to eliminate hidden benefits," Steyn said.
He said former finance minister Chris Liebenberg had told the commission the number of MPs should be reduced to 300 from 400. "The evidence was persuasive," Steyn added.
He said the pension system for politicians under the former apartheid government needed to be revised because it "exposed the taxpayer to the risk of meeting open-ended, generous commitments".

The commission recommended that an independent assessor be appointed to monitor the work of individual members of parliament, partly to meet criticism that the job was a "gravy train" of undeserved perks and benefits.
The recommendations have been handed to Mandela but no decision on them has been announced yet.
